newsitem.title: USA: Japan needs to avoid sustained surplus rise -- Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs to avoid sustained surplus rise -- Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Wednesday said it was "very important" that Japan achieve domestic demand-led economic growth and avoid a sustained increase in its trade surplus.
"I think that it's very important for the world that that objective be met," Rubin told public television's Nightly Business Report.
He added that he expects that topic to be discussed in Denver, where leaders of the industrial world will gather for a June 20-22 summit.

"I'm sure we'll have some discussion of how significant increases in Japan's external surpluses ... could reverberate around the world, undermine growth in other countries and also set off a backlash against trade liberalization," Rubin said.
The Japanese government reported on Wednesday that the country's customs-cleared trade surplus jumped by more than 200 percent in May from a year earlier.
Rubin told Nightly Business Report that the United States also has an "enormously strong interest" in having a strong Europe.

"The question is exactly what Europe needs to do in order to have sustained economic growth, which they really have not had at a significant level for quite some time, and have a regeneration of job creation," the Treasury chief said.
He said that European nations need to tackle their structural economic problems and make their labor and capital markets more flexible.
